title: Stop Converting Files One by One. There's a Better Way.
description: Batch file conversion saves hours of repetitive work. Here's how FileTools handles dozens of files at once — no software install needed.
excerpt: Dragging files one at a time into a converter is a productivity killer. Batch conversion fixes that.
content:
You've been there. Thirty PDFs that need to become PNGs. A folder of HEIC photos your client can't open. Word documents that should've been PDFs yesterday.

Most people solve this file by file. Open a converter, upload, wait, download, repeat. It works, but it's slow and mind-numbing.

## The batch approach

[FileTools](https://filetools.eu) lets you drop multiple files at once. Select your target format, hit convert, download everything. No account required, no software to install.

The entire process runs in your browser. Your files don't sit on someone's server for days — they're processed and cleaned up.

## When batch conversion actually matters

The real value shows up in workflows. A photographer exporting a shoot to JPEG. A lawyer converting a stack of documents to PDF/A for archival. A developer resizing 40 icons for an app release.

These aren't edge cases. They're Tuesday.

[FileTools](https://filetools.eu) supports the formats people actually use: PDF, DOCX, PNG, JPG, WEBP, SVG, and more. No obscure format gatekeeping.

## Pair it with other tools

If you're already using [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) for video dubbing, you know the value of automating repetitive media tasks. Same principle here — let the tool do the boring part.

Working on room redesigns with [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io)? Export your before/after comparisons through [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) to get consistent formats for presentations.

## The bottom line

Batch conversion isn't exciting. It's just faster. And faster means you move on to work that actually needs your brain.
